// p3stdin is F5's stdin witness (Burroughs #1240): an ordinary Go program that reads all of os.Stdin.
// Built for the fork's GOOS=wasip3, os.Stdin is read-via-stream read through the runtime's netpoller.
// It prints what p3cat (a Rust wasm32-wasip3 std program) prints for the same bytes: the byte count, a
// checksum, the line count and the first line.
//
// The first read waits with no timer pending, so the runtime's wait is netpoll's unbounded one. A
// goroutine that sleeps for an hour is then started, so every later read waits in netpoll with a timer
// in the set, and stdin's event ends that wait before the timer does.
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"time"
)

func main() {
	first := make([]byte, 4096)
	n, err := os.Stdin.Read(first)
	if err != nil && err != io.EOF {
		fail(err)
	}
	go time.Sleep(time.Hour)
	rest, err := io.ReadAll(os.Stdin)
	if err != nil {
		fail(err)
	}
	buf := append(first[:n], rest...)
	var sum uint32
	for _, b := range buf {
		sum = sum*31 + uint32(b)
	}
	fmt.Printf("p3stdin: read %d bytes, checksum %08x, %d lines\n", len(buf), sum, bytes.Count(buf, []byte("\n")))
	line, _, _ := bytes.Cut(buf, []byte("\n"))
	fmt.Printf("p3stdin: first line: %s\n", line)
}

func fail(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "p3stdin: reading stdin failed:", err)
	os.Exit(1)
}
